name: Ts’ui T’u
bio: Ts’ui T’u was a T’ang poet who took his degree in AD 888, according to the chronology of poets in The Jade Mountain.
The poems here are Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu’s versions in The Jade Mountain (1929), given with the poet’s name as spelled here.

poems.title: On New Year's Eve
poems.author: Ts’ui T’u
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Farther and farther from the three Pa Roads,
I have come three thousand miles, anxious and watchful,
Through pale snow-patches in the jagged night-mountains —
A stranger with a lonely lantern shaken in the wind.
. . . Separation from my kin
Binds me closer to my servants —
Yet how I dread, so far adrift,
New Year's Day, tomorrow morning!

poems.title: A Solitary Wildgoose
poems.author: Ts’ui T’u
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Line after line has flown back over the border.
Where are you headed all by yourself?
In the evening rain you call to them —
And slowly you alight on an icy pond.
The low wet clouds move faster than you
Along the wall toward the cold moon.
. . . If they caught you in a net or with a shot,
Would it be worse than flying alone?
